A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VCR task and VCR-WIKI dataset. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renamed models and relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, image-removal ablations and a seven-volunteer human study, with additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original model and human evaluations and adds model comparisons, benchmark-correlation analysis and transfer experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The caption construction, filtering, masking and restoration procedures remain unchanged. Fine-tuning Qwen2-VL extends the existing LoRA recipe to another evaluated model. Appendix D's architectural and chain-of-thought suggestions are future directions, not implemented changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates VCR-WIKI's English/Chinese and easy/hard configurations. v3 retains these and adds OKVQA training and evaluation across broader tasks, including mathematical reasoning, diagram understanding, chart QA and OCR-related benchmarks in Table 7. The 23-benchmark correlation analysis further expands empirical coverage beyond caption restoration.

E2.justification: v3 adds numerous evaluated models, including Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Reka Core, Qwen2-VL, Cambrian-1, Pixtral and Llama-3.2. Idefics2 and InternVL-V1.5 are replaced by Idefics3 and InternVL-V2; Chinese comparisons now include additional GPT and Claude models. Table 7 adds OKVQA-fine-tuned controls. TextMonkey becomes Monkey with the same checkpoint link and retained scores, so that change is a relabeling.

E3.justification: New protocols include correlation analysis of 38 VLMs across 23 benchmarks, K-means clustering and PCA visualization, plus comparisons of unfine-tuned, OKVQA-fine-tuned and VCR-fine-tuned models across tasks and languages. The existing VCR metrics, dataset splits, LoRA training budget, 100/500-case appendix evaluations and human-study design are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B add analyses of whether VCR measures capabilities distinct from other benchmarks. Appendix D/Table 7 adds cross-language and cross-task transfer analysis with alternative fine-tuning controls. Section 4.4 also examines model size and resolution. Existing image-removal and fine-tuning analyses remain, with Qwen2-VL added to the latter.

E5.justification: v1 Table 3 supplies bootstrap standard deviations for full-test fine-tuned results. Their retained exact-match means appear in v3 Figure 5 and Table 7 without uncertainty estimates. Bootstrap reporting remains in the other VCR result tables, including the smaller-subset fine-tuning results, and human-study standard deviations are unchanged. No new seed or repeated-run counts are disclosed.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive model, correlation, fine-tuning and transfer results while retaining many earlier means and all human scores. In the matched first-500 English-hard VI+TEI comparison, newly added Qwen2-VL achieves 76.27% exact match versus CogVLM2's retained 41.74%, changing the untuned open-model ranking (v1 Table 6; v3 Table 5). Full-test fine-tuned TEI-only and Jaccard entries from v1 Table 3 are omitted, although VI+TEI exact-match means survive in Figure 5/Table 7.

T1.justification: The task representation, n-gram matching and exact-match/Jaccard definitions retain their mathematical meaning. The piecewise exact-match formula becomes equivalent indicator notation. Neither version contains theoretical results or proofs that are substantively revised; the new correlation and PCA material is empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, four listed contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing VCR, its generation pipeline and multilingual dataset, demonstrating a human-model performance gap, and finding inconsistent fine-tuning benefits. The added conclusion sentence about a controllable testbed elaborates the existing benchmark design.

C2.justification: v3 expands brief architectural speculation into detailed hypotheses about image partitioning, token filtering and loss of pixel-level cues. It qualifies v1's suggestion that scaling may help through size/resolution comparisons, interprets benchmark correlations as evidence of distinctive reasoning requirements, and adds strong transfer/generalization interpretations. Appendix D also discusses aspect-ratio limitations and possible pretraining or chain-of-thought remedies.

D1.justification: v3 adds precise API identifiers/testing dates, checkpoint links for additional models, encoder-resolution details and a direct transformation-script reference. Existing LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, dataset licensing and general code access remain. However, it drops v1's explicit disclosure that the main comparison evaluates open models on 5,000 cases and closed models on 500; this is a documentation loss, not evidence of changed sample sizes.

R1.justification: v3 removes the masked-modeling and standalone scene-text-detection discussions, including associated BERT/iGPT/MAE coverage, while adding recent VLMs, multimodal encoders and chain-of-thought literature. Section 4.3 and Appendix B introduce quantitative positioning against other benchmarks. These changes substantively reshape the research context beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The existing experimental discussion is extensively rewritten from open/closed-model groupings into seven thematic findings. v3 inserts a benchmark-relationship subsection, reorganizes supplementary material into Appendices A-D, shortens related work and adds a question-and-answer discussion. Widespread copyediting and compressed metric explanations accompany this substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 adds a human-restoration illustration, benchmark PCA plot, correlation heatmap, fine-tuning bar charts and transfer table. Comparison tables gain an explicit open/closed-source column and revised highlighting; model specifications move to Appendix C. The original pipeline figure is retained and renumbered, while Figure 5 partly redisplays existing results. The document also adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through broader matched comparisons and direct tests of benchmark distinctiveness and transfer. Table 7 newly demonstrates cross-language benefits, including English-trained CogVLM2 improving Chinese-easy exact match from 9.15 to 42.55. However, its broad generalization claims overstate mixed external-benchmark outcomes, while lost main-evaluation sample-size disclosure and full-test fine-tuning uncertainty reduce transparency. The added evidence produces a useful but limited net quality improvement.
